Combining them increases drowsiness and can worsen sleep quality rather than improve it.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXDuFjmVwW-ASQ8q4OAFOkskX_1GPp-3YYNt6G1vFnvilbbMgw7PyzSNPtT3ZSQWsxMWNk4llsOz93ZEqtAJgA5NAEIcsXWFpeknJOGg1RZqRo-kI6kL7gE3ytj1TyK2sZrpNKzuodxXd4JIlX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXxp77nAeIC2Df_U7PufP5V9R3Hw5k9gyac1jYMFYLU2Ev3sIaUNIgf_jUoWLQlHTnQ7QZ1zCrnuLtEeixAb89KSG5ph495i66J0uKsqWVse05Rwt5UyQRuNlnDYqCA9UJ4IW4uAFttl0UMdwViAgmpm8O7Iq8)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX4p695MRJaKv3YxwVgCVJaPpu6MjEXDKDDbUeMHvHxZ_uAmtkS5rFH0ri3xUy4Q3cefOa-SCoN9dTIkJP8Ay2NiRRaDAiYTnFyk1vebTee4T97wo46IHOzoSIzZmOIi5a)

### Key Risks and Effects

- **Heightened sedation:** Both substances slow central nervous system activity, which can cause excessive drowsiness, dizziness, grogginess, impaired thinking, or trouble waking up.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXxp77nAeIC2Df_U7PufP5V9R3Hw5k9gyac1jYMFYLU2Ev3sIaUNIgf_jUoWLQlHTnQ7QZ1zCrnuLtEeixAb89KSG5ph495i66J0uKsqWVse05Rwt5UyQRuNlnDYqCA9UJ4IW4uAFttl0UMdwViAgmpm8O7Iq8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXDuFjmVwW-ASQ8q4OAFOkskX_1GPp-3YYNt6G1vFnvilbbMgw7PyzSNPtT3ZSQWsxMWNk4llsOz93ZEqtAJgA5NAEIcsXWFpeknJOGg1RZqRo-kI6kL7gE3ytj1TyK2sZrpNKzuodxXd4JIlX)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1zYF9L_TDY-t2Vb2GzFYWXCp3Ct765EVb8W4q0_6YXTR5Jm1uE21r3bAXpqTjfCL3oaojg5E21XxZMEHBOTkXFyKNgRf3G-GVXtGQ2HWrzXbR-DLW5XRQrqs5L6K0wD4LEczWdtO24sN23fYPy_Dqzc-3LHn0wlAMXcZUHKt)
- **Worse sleep architecture:** Alcohol suppresses REM sleep and causes nighttime awakenings , and melatonin does not reliably fix alcohol-disrupted sleep.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXDuFjmVwW-ASQ8q4OAFOkskX_1GPp-3YYNt6G1vFnvilbbMgw7PyzSNPtT3ZSQWsxMWNk4llsOz93ZEqtAJgA5NAEIcsXWFpeknJOGg1RZqRo-kI6kL7gE3ytj1TyK2sZrpNKzuodxXd4JIlX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX1Xw_RXgUykYET_aqZhHVZFFodCKkPsJyGClRz3wm-t1uPm4Q9dZckf-T5t3i-K8xxd7YxAcKDU5hYrWMUgUIqGJdsNd-rYTg-XDlGQl6Z4UbdZQZoJfapaAPjQiMSsfEbYGAcNBD)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX4p695MRJaKv3YxwVgCVJaPpu6MjEXDKDDbUeMHvHxZ_uAmtkS5rFH0ri3xUy4Q3cefOa-SCoN9dTIkJP8Ay2NiRRaDAiYTnFyk1vebTee4T97wo46IHOzoSIzZmOIi5a)
- **Breathing and fall risks:** Relaxed airway muscles can worsen snoring or sleep apnea, and extra sedation raises fall risks—especially for older adults.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1zYF9L_TDY-t2Vb2GzFYWXCp3Ct765EVb8W4q0_6YXTR5Jm1uE21r3bAXpqTjfCL3oaojg5E21XxZMEHBOTkXFyKNgRf3G-GVXtGQ2HWrzXbR-DLW5XRQrqs5L6K0wD4LEczWdtO24sN23fYPy_Dqzc-3LHn0wlAMXcZUHKt)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXxp77nAeIC2Df_U7PufP5V9R3Hw5k9gyac1jYMFYLU2Ev3sIaUNIgf_jUoWLQlHTnQ7QZ1zCrnuLtEeixAb89KSG5ph495i66J0uKsqWVse05Rwt5UyQRuNlnDYqCA9UJ4IW4uAFttl0UMdwViAgmpm8O7Iq8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX1Xw_RXgUykYET_aqZhHVZFFodCKkPsJyGClRz3wm-t1uPm4Q9dZckf-T5t3i-K8xxd7YxAcKDU5hYrWMUgUIqGJdsNd-rYTg-XDlGQl6Z4UbdZQZoJfapaAPjQiMSsfEbYGAcNBD)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXOmM4POvC7OKzTTvzdTY9VfCBu-es4ktnmJ5XJmKCP0-aKnYnwNM1puSaJllZyrdA6scCo6Qai90esxjhOvwQPNPXWG294EygYcA6z5ieEFAmxa8TABCbK4U1U504oA1nUOzZMAhh)
- **Other possible side effects:** People occasionally report headaches, anxiety, vivid dreams, or stomach upset.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXOmM4POvC7OKzTTvzdTY9VfCBu-es4ktnmJ5XJmKCP0-aKnYnwNM1puSaJllZyrdA6scCo6Qai90esxjhOvwQPNPXWG294EygYcA6z5ieEFAmxa8TABCbK4U1U504oA1nUOzZMAhh)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)

For more details on potential side effects and label guidance, see the [Sleep Foundation](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXxp77nAeIC2Df_U7PufP5V9R3Hw5k9gyac1jYMFYLU2Ev3sIaUNIgf_jUoWLQlHTnQ7QZ1zCrnuLtEeixAb89KSG5ph495i66J0uKsqWVse05Rwt5UyQRuNlnDYqCA9UJ4IW4uAFttl0UMdwViAgmpm8O7Iq8) and [Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA) . On [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF11K9NaGN0Pfac5OAIaGH-Lt1diHBYeeBE4CZJ-EXhHwvtM3TWz7pSt1jJHJ8DXDzTOxyGqxtZH1ZcAaG0EzSopYf7ZIEsYVwQfPi3Q6wZ4wYkUBVtLbqdXnoDdEbX6gGbRdgbbsWZJ-Vp0FIa66zAnARts_XensORPmBFTLJ8n2nxNjdLsm9noklhom1XVvtSstqhl6o) , opinions are mixed: many users warn against combining them due to next-day grogginess or disrupted sleep, while a few suggest a low dose with a couple of drinks feels mild since melatonin is naturally produced in the body.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXxp77nAeIC2Df_U7PufP5V9R3Hw5k9gyac1jYMFYLU2Ev3sIaUNIgf_jUoWLQlHTnQ7QZ1zCrnuLtEeixAb89KSG5ph495i66J0uKsqWVse05Rwt5UyQRuNlnDYqCA9UJ4IW4uAFttl0UMdwViAgmpm8O7Iq8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF11K9NaGN0Pfac5OAIaGH-Lt1diHBYeeBE4CZJ-EXhHwvtM3TWz7pSt1jJHJ8DXDzTOxyGqxtZH1ZcAaG0EzSopYf7ZIEsYVwQfPi3Q6wZ4wYkUBVtLbqdXnoDdEbX6gGbRdgbbsWZJ-Vp0FIa66zAnARts_XensORPmBFTLJ8n2nxNjdLsm9noklhom1XVvtSstqhl6o)

### Practical Guidance

- **If you drink:** Skip your melatonin dose that night and wait until you have been alcohol-free for about 24 hours before taking it again.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXDuFjmVwW-ASQ8q4OAFOkskX_1GPp-3YYNt6G1vFnvilbbMgw7PyzSNPtT3ZSQWsxMWNk4llsOz93ZEqtAJgA5NAEIcsXWFpeknJOGg1RZqRo-kI6kL7gE3ytj1TyK2sZrpNKzuodxXd4JIlX)
- **If you take melatonin:** Because melatonin typically clears the body in roughly 5 to 10 hours, some guidance suggests waiting at least a few hours after a nighttime dose before having a drink the next day—though avoiding alcohol when managing sleep is generally more effective.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXDuFjmVwW-ASQ8q4OAFOkskX_1GPp-3YYNt6G1vFnvilbbMgw7PyzSNPtT3ZSQWsxMWNk4llsOz93ZEqtAJgA5NAEIcsXWFpeknJOGg1RZqRo-kI6kL7gE3ytj1TyK2sZrpNKzuodxXd4JIlX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)
- **Check medications:** Melatonin can interact with certain drugs (such as blood thinners, immunosuppressants, diabetes medications, or birth control), so check with a pharmacist or doctor if you take regular medications.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX5bPmn8GqnVYlK7Rf84RyZAOSbXi840ocxpz1hJ7n6kVgsmqrDqSgTYUeR-y3zT8nvIAaCv0J4EGK3Q3jTcO3sAqVLMjrBvCks2qnfoldlLDEEO_uZ3yK-BCi995lL7Tl3g4KXwzgwBZO4AKzuA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1zYF9L_TDY-t2Vb2GzFYWXCp3Ct765EVb8W4q0_6YXTR5Jm1uE21r3bAXpqTjfCL3oaojg5E21XxZMEHBOTkXFyKNgRf3G-GVXtGQ2HWrzXbR-DLW5XRQrqs5L6K0wD4LEczWdtO24sN23fYPy_Dqzc-3LHn0wlAMXcZUHKt)

items.text: Heightened sedation: Both substances slow central nervous system activity, which can cause excessive drowsiness, dizziness, grogginess, impaired thinking, or trouble waking up. Worse sleep architecture: Alcohol suppresses REM sleep and causes nighttime awakenings, and melatonin does not reliably fix alcohol-disrupted sleep. items.title: Practical Guidance
items.text: If you drink: Skip your melatonin dose that night and wait until you have been alcohol-free for about 24 hours before taking it again. If you take melatonin: Because melatonin typically clears the body in roughly 5 to 10 hours, some guidance suggests waiting at least a few hours after a nighttime dose before having a drink the next day—though avoiding alcohol when managing sleep is generally more effective. Check medications: Melatonin can interact with certain drugs (such as blood thinners, immunosuppressants, diabetes medications, or birth control), so check with a pharmacist or doctor if you take regular medications.
